digest.en: Zelenskyy confirms Starlink is back to full capacity in Ukraine after Starshield disruptions. Simultaneously, Iran vows apocalyptic war if the U.S. strikes again. Kim Jong-un crossed a new bridge into China.

articles.title: This nurse has cared for more than 100 dying patients – what they taught her about having a ‘happy
articles.summary: Mariam Jumaat, a home palliative care nurse, has cared for over 100 dying patients. She previously believed good nursing meant curing illness and avoided end-of-life care. Now she helps patients spend their final days at home. Her work focuses on comfort and allowing them to be surrounded by loved ones. This shift in perspective redefined her approach to patient care.

articles.title: After Starshield Disruptions, Zelenskyy Says Satellite Communications Now Fully Functional
articles.summary: Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed on October 24 that Starshield and Starlink systems are fully operational. The satellite communications, developed by SpaceX, had been disrupted for over a week. This outage limited Ukraine's defensive operations during the period. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on October 24 that the Starshield and Starlink satellite systems were back to normal operations. Disruptions in the communications systems, developed by Elon Musk's SpaceX company, had limited Ukraine's defensive operations for over a week.

articles.title: Iran vows ‘apocalyptic war’ if U.S. strikes again
articles.summary: Iranian officials warned they would target Persian Gulf states if the United States launches new strikes. Previous retaliatory phases saw Iran hit American military bases and regional energy infrastructure. The threat aims to deter further escalation in the ongoing conflict. Iranian officials have warned in recent days that they would retaliate by targeting Persian Gulf countries in the event of renewed U. S.

articles.title: Iran Speaker to skip BRICS meet, as Iran seeks bilateral air route for ‘humanitarian aid’ from India
articles.summary: Iran's parliament speaker will skip the upcoming BRICS summit. Tehran is negotiating a bilateral air route with India for medical supplies. Iranian authorities claim humanitarian aid is exempt from U. S. sanctions, while New Delhi suggests routing cargo through a third country. Iran Air not allowed to fly medicines directly from India to Tehran, due to fear of U. sanctions; India says medicines can be taken through a third country; Tehran says humanitarian aid is exempted from sanctions.

articles.title: Bipartisan US Lawmakers Push Back On Trump's Russia Policy, Vow Support For Ukraine
articles.summary: A bipartisan group of US lawmakers challenged President Trump's easing of Russian energy import restrictions. They demanded guarantees that Ukraine retains access to critical American military and intelligence support. The move signals growing congressional resistance to the administration's shifting foreign policy stance on the conflict. A bipartisan group of US lawmakers is stepping up efforts to defend Ukraine, challenging President Donald Trump’s decision to ease restrictions on Russian energy imports and demanding guarantees that Kyiv will retain access to critical American military and intelligence support.

articles.title: Kim Jong-un crosses newly opened bridge into China
articles.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un crossed the newly opened New Yalu River Bridge into China. He arrived in the border city of Dandong to meet senior Communist party officials. The visit marked the inauguration of the new crossing and signaled a push to expand bilateral cooperation between the two nations. North Korean leader travels over New Yalu River Bridge to meet senior Communist party memberKim Jong-un has visited China, inaugurating a bridge that connects the two countries and saying he hopes to expand cooperation with his neighbour. The North Korean leader arrived in the Chinese border city of Dandong on Saturday after crossing the New Yalu River Bridge, according to South Korea’s unification.

articles.title: Starlink back to 'the level ⁠we need' in Ukraine, Zelenskyy says
articles.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that the Starlink satellite system has returned to the operational speed Ukraine requires. The network had slowed for over a week, which impaired Kyiv's ability to defend against Russian attacks. The restoration of full bandwidth is critical for maintaining Ukraine's air defense and communications infrastructure. The Starlink satellite system is back to operating at the speed Ukraine needs after slowing down for more than a week, damaging Kyiv's ability to defend itself from Russian attacks, Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said.

articles.title: Women ‘first to suffer’ under siege, first to step up as frontline responders in Sudan
articles.summary: Tahani Al-Numeiri in Khartoum mistook the initial explosions for wedding celebrations on 15 April 2023. The Rapid Support Forces had just opened fire on the army. Women in Sudan now serve as frontline responders during the siege. They face immediate danger while managing critical aid distribution. The conflict has forced them into roles previously held by men. Their work sustains communities under active bombardment.

articles.title: Green batteries built on dirty dealings in Indonesia
articles.summary: Leaked documents reveal Harita Group paid for goodwill on Obi island to secure nickel for electric vehicle batteries. The Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project published the files on October 22. These payments facilitated mining operations that supply a growing share of global battery production. A growing share of the world’s electric-vehicle batteries contains nickel from Obi, an Indonesian island where the mining company Harita Group has long paid for goodwill, according to alleged leaked documents published on October 22 by the Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project (OCCRP).

articles.title: China bets refitted destroyers can hold line in US numbers race
articles.summary: China is refitting older destroyers to maintain fleet mass against the United States. The People's Liberation Army Navy completed extensive midlife upgrades on surface combatants this month. This approach prioritizes preserving numbers over purely qualitative technological modernization in naval warfare. Recent midlife upgrades to China’s older surface combatants highlight an ongoing debate over whether preserving naval fleet mass provides an operational edge over purely qualitative technological modernization in naval warfare.

articles.title: Why ultra‑Orthodox parties will decide Netanyahu’s electoral fate
articles.summary: Israeli authorities detained dozens of Haredi men on 20 October 2026, a week before national elections. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemned the draft evasion arrests as unacceptable. The incident highlights the political leverage ultra-Orthodox parties hold over Netanyahu's electoral prospects following a 2024 court ruling on military service exemptions. On October 20, 2026, a week before Israel’s elections, dozens of men were detained on suspicion of evading the draft – arrests that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called “unacceptable.” The young men attend ultra-Orthodox, or Haredi, religious schools, whose students were long exempt from the military service mandatory for most Israelis.

articles.title: White House Says Melania Trump Brokers Localized Cease-Fire For Occupied Ukrainian City
articles.summary: Melania Trump brokered a localized cease-fire for Oleshky, a Russian-occupied Ukrainian city. Kyiv confirmed preparations for humanitarian corridors. Non-military teams will visit residents to coordinate civilian evacuations. An American media organization will document the process. US First Lady Melania Trump has brokered a localized cease-fire between Russia and Ukraine for the Russian-occupied southern Ukrainian city of Oleshky, with Kyiv confirming preparations for an operation to establish humanitarian corridors and evacuate civilians.

articles.title: Every Day We 'Wake Up Poorer': Iranians Battle Economic Woes
articles.summary: Iran’s economy faces severe strain from mismanagement, sanctions, and war. Citizens report waking up poorer daily. The cost-of-living crisis forces changes in diet, social habits, and life choices. Basic affordability is eroding across the population. Battered by mismanagement, sanctions, and war, Iran’s economy is in deep trouble. The cost-of-living crisis is forcing people to change what they eat, how they socialize, and what they can afford to do with their lives.

articles.title: Mystery over source of Ebola infection in Nigeria fuels concern about spread of virus
articles.summary: Health officials are investigating how Nigeria’s first Ebola patient in over a decade contracted the virus. The patient is the wife of a Swiss diplomat who traveled in Uganda. The outbreak has reached a fourth African country, raising concerns about further spread. Switzerland says patient is wife of Swiss diplomat and believed to have contracted virus while travelling in UgandaHealth officials across Africa are racing to determine how Nigeria’s first Ebola patient ⁠in more than a decade ⁠became infected, amid fears ​the outbreak could spread further after reaching a fourth African country. articles.title: An Arctic Traffic Jam Highlights Doubts Over Russia's Northern Sea Route To China
articles.summary: Russian officials face growing doubts about the Northern Sea Route's viability as a reliable trade corridor to China. The Kremlin invested heavily in the route, betting that retreating Arctic ice would open a path beyond Ukrainian drone strikes and European naval interdiction. Recent traffic congestion along the waterway has exposed the practical difficulties of navigating through remaining ice. The route remains a strategic priority, but operational challenges are complicating the timeline for consistent commercial use.

articles.title: Iran’s mountain shelters offer Taiwan a China survival playbook
articles.summary: Iran is repairing its Eagle 44 airbase in Hormozgan province after recent strikes. The subterranean facility demonstrates the value of hardened mountain shelters against precision firepower. This recovery offers a survival playbook for air forces facing superior adversaries. Iran’s rapid post-strike recovery of its Eagle 44 airbase proves that hardened mountain shelters remain a decisive shield against precision firepower, transforming how inferior air forces survive and deter superior adversaries.

articles.title: Serbia's Vucic Faces Biggest Election Challenge Yet Amid Fraud Fears
articles.summary: Aleksandar Vucic faces his toughest parliamentary election challenge in fourteen years on October 25. An opposition movement born from student protests threatens his long-standing dominance. Growing concerns persist over whether the voting process will be conducted fairly. After 14 years dominating Serbian politics, Aleksandar Vucic faces the biggest challenge to his rule in parliamentary elections on October 25 from an opposition movement that has sprung from mass student protests.

articles.title: US-China AI race turning ASEAN neutrality into a liability
articles.summary: The U. S.-China AI competition is eroding ASEAN’s traditional neutrality. Southeast Asian nations previously leveraged ties with both powers for economic gain. Competing technology networks now force governments to choose sides, reducing their diplomatic flexibility and strategic room for maneuver. For decades, Southeast Asia has turned great-power rivalry to an economic advantage. By maintaining healthy ties with Washington and Beijing, ASEAN governments attracted investment, expanded trade and preserved room for diplomatic maneuver.

articles.title: Xi’s peace principles offer little cover for China in Africa
articles.summary: Jihadist factions JNIM and ISSP clashed near Gonadaouri in Burkina Faso on October 9. The fight occurred in Oudalan province close to the Malian border. This violence highlights the limits of China’s peace principles in the region. Beijing’s diplomatic framework offers little practical cover for its interests there. The conflict underscores the persistent instability in the Sahel. On October 9, fighters from two jihadist groups clashed near Gonadaouri, in Burkina Faso’s Oudalan province, not far from the Malian border.

articles.title: Deportations And Jail Terms Leave Tajik Dissidents In Europe Fearing For Their Future
articles.summary: Tajik dissidents report feeling abandoned by Western nations following recent deportations. Several opposition figures were expelled from Germany and other European countries. They face imprisonment upon returning to Tajikistan. Exiled activists now fear losing the diplomatic support they previously relied on for protection. The deportation of several Tajik opposition figures from Germany and other European countries, and their subsequent imprisonment, have heightened fears among Tajik oppositionists in exile.

articles.title: Alberta welcomed migrant workers. Now, it wants to restrict their rights
articles.summary: Alberta plans to restrict rights for migrant workers despite previously welcoming them. Vanesa Ortiz, a Mexican resident in Calgary, criticized the move as scapegoating. She argued such measures will not lower the cost of living. ‘Scapegoating non-permanent residents is not going to lower the cost of living,’ Vanesa Ortiz saysWhen Vanesa Ortiz came to Calgary from Mexico, she found herself in a city gripped by winter.

articles.title: Ukraine Cuts Chinese Drone Dependence, But Critical Gaps Remain
articles.summary: Ukraine has sharply reduced its reliance on Chinese drone components since 2022. However, critical parts remain difficult to replace at scale and cost. This leaves a persistent dependency on Beijing for essential military hardware. In 2022, Ukraine relied almost entirely on Chinese components for its military drones. While that dependency has now been drastically reduced, Ukraine still relies on Beijing for essential parts that remain difficult to replace at the necessary scale and cost.

articles.title: When Big Tech becomes a tool of state control in Kenya
articles.summary: Access Now's 2025 report documented 313 global internet shutdowns. Africa saw 30 shutdowns across 15 countries during the period. Protests served as the primary trigger for these outages. Elections followed as the second most common cause for state-imposed connectivity cuts. Access Now's 2025 report found that at least 313 shutdowns were implemented globally, and that in Africa the Internet was shut down 30 times in 15 countries, with protests the leading trigger, followed by elections.

articles.title: Severely ill ICE detainees face imminent deportation to unknown African states, advocates say
articles.summary: Families report ICE is deporting severely ill detainees from Florida jails. Flights to unknown African countries are scheduled for Wednesday. Advocates say the detainees have no ties to these destinations despite worsening medical conditions. Flights to third countries where the detainees have no ties are scheduled as early as Wednesday, relatives detailRelatives of gravely ill detainees at two Florida immigration jails say authorities are about to deport their loved ones to unknown countries in Africa despite worsening medical conditions. Flights are scheduled as early as Wednesday, according to the families and the immigration advocac.

articles.title: दक्षिण प्रशांत महासागर में आया 7.2 तीव्रता का भूकंप, सुनामी की चेतावनी जारी
articles.summary: वानुअतु के पास 24 अक्टूबर को 7.2 तीव्रता का भूकंप आया। प्रशांत सुनामी चेतावनी केंद्र ने 300 किमी दायरे में खतरनाक लहरों की चेतावनी जारी की। दक्षिण प्रशांत महासागर में स्थित वानुअतु द्वीपसमूह के पास शनिवार, 24 अक्टूबर को 7.2 तीव्रता का शक्तिशाली भूकंप आया. इसके बाद प्रशांत सुनामी चेतावनी केंद्र ने सुनामी की चेतावनी जारी की. केंद्र के अनुसार, भूकंप के केंद्र से 300 किलोमीटर के दायरे में स्थित तटीय इलाकों में खतरनाक समुद्री लहरें उठने की आशंका है.

articles.summary: ट्रंप ने कहा कि ईरान से लौटते अमेरिकी युद्धपोत क्यूबा के पास रुक सकते हैं। उन्होंने फ्लोरिडा में रैली को संबोधित करते हुए यह बात कही। यह टिप्पणी मध्यावधि चुनावों से पहले की गई। Trump statement on Cuba: अमेरिकी राष्ट्रपति डोनाल्ड ट्रंप ने एकबार फिर क्यूबा पर कब्जे जैसी बात कही है। ट्रंप ने बीते शुक्रवार को कहा कि ईरान युद्ध से लौट रहे अमेरिकी युद्धपोत क्यूबा के पास कुछ देर के लिए रुक सकते हैं।

articles.title: भारत-पाकिस्तान संघर्ष पर डोनाल्ड ट्रंप का फिर बड़ा दावा, बोले- व्यापार बंद करने की धमकी से रुकवाई
articles.summary: ट्रंप ने दावा किया कि 250 प्रतिशत टैरिफ की धमकी ने भारत-पाकिस्तान संघर्ष रोकने में मदद की। उन्होंने फ्लोरिडा में रैली में यह बात कही। दोनों पक्षों ने तुरंत सैन्य गतिविधियां बंद कर दीं। Donald Trump Claim on India-Pakistan Conflict: अमेरिकी राष्ट्रपति डोनाल्ड ट्रंप ने एक बार फिर दावा किया है कि भारत और पाकिस्तान के बीच सैन्य संघर्ष को रोकने में उनकी भूमिका थी।
